[Brief summary integrating predisposing, precipitating, perpetuating, and protective factors contributing to the current presentation.]
- Predisposing: Family history of migraines; no documented prior mental health history
- Precipitating: Acute migraine-type headache with nausea, photophobia; health anxiety triggered by symptoms

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Address each principal problem identified in Clinical Assessment - Section A. Add additional problems as relevant.)

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Relieve acute migraine symptoms; reduce health-related anxiety; minimize impact on work
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Confirm migraine-type headache; initiate appropriate acute treatment; discuss potential prophylaxis if recurrent; provide reassurance and education
- Actions (Patient):
  - Maintain headache diary
  - Use acute analgesics as recommended (paracetamol or co-codamol; dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Seek urgent care if red flags or symptoms worsen
  - Return for follow-up in 1 week
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide migraine-focused assessment and reassurance
  - Discuss and initiate acute treatment plan (paracetamol, NSAIDs) and consider prophylaxis if headaches persist
  - Recommend headache diary and follow-up appointment in ~1 week
  - Advise red-flag instructions and when to return urgently

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Manage work-related stress; reduce health-related worry
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Acknowledge psychosocial stressors; discuss coping/resources; monitor impact on headaches
- Actions (Patient):
  - Consider basic stress management approaches; engage in follow-up
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide general support; discuss possible stress management resources; consider referral to mental health services if symptoms persist

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes
- Topics Covered:
  - Migraine vs red flags; headache diary; acute treatment options; plan for follow-up
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Headache worsens or does not respond to medications
  - Neck pain worsens
  - Weakness in arms/legs or vision changes
  - New neurological symptoms
  - Fever or systemic signs
- Coping Strategies:
  - Headache diary to identify triggers
  - Rest as needed
  - Use of prescribed analgesics and escalation plan; return if symptoms worsen or fail to improve
